title: The Ultimate Pilot Challenge
description: Test your mastery of the most difficult FAR and AIM regulations. Only for the experts!

questions.question: Under FAR 91.175, which of the following is NOT a required visual reference to descend below DA/MDA?
options: The approach light system (descending to 100 feet above TDZE)
The touchdown zone or touchdown zone markings
questions.explanation: Taxiway lead-in lights are NOT a listed visual reference in 91.175(c)(3) that permits descent below DA/MDA. Permitted items include the threshold, threshold markings/lights, runway end identifier lights, visual approach slope indicator, touchdown zone/markings/lights, and runway/markings/lights.

questions.question: For Special VFR operations at night, what requirements must be met?
options: The pilot must be instrument rated
The aircraft must be instrument equipped
Both the pilot and aircraft must be instrument qualified
Special VFR is not permitted at night
questions.explanation: FAR 91.157(b)(4) states that for Special VFR at night, the person must meet the requirements for Instrument Flight under Part 61 AND the aircraft must be equipped for IFR flight.

questions.question: What is the specific cloud clearance requirement for VFR flight in Class G airspace at night, below 1,200 feet AGL?
options: 500 feet below, 1,000 feet above, 2,000 feet horizontal
1,000 feet below, 1,000 feet above, 1 mile horizontal
questions.explanation: Normally Class G below 1,200 AGL is 'Clear of Clouds' during the day. However, AT NIGHT (regardless of altitude in Class G), the requirement increases to 3 statute miles visibility and 500 below, 1000 above, 2000 horizontal cloud clearance (FAR 91.155).

questions.question: When is an alternate airport NOT required for an IFR flight plan (the '1-2-3 Rule')?
options: If the destination has an instrument approach
If from 1 hour before to 1 hour after ETA, the ceiling is at least 2,000 feet and visibility is at least 3 statute miles
If from 1 hour before to 1 hour after ETA, the ceiling is at least 1,000 feet and visibility is at least 2 statute miles
If the destination has a TAF
questions.explanation: An alternate is always required unless the destination has an IAP AND weather reports forecast, from 1 hour before to 1 hour after ETA, a ceiling of at least 2,000 feet above airport elevation and visibility of at least 3 statute miles.

questions.question: According to the AIM, what does a 'Steady Green' light gun signal mean to an aircraft in flight?
questions.explanation: For an aircraft in flight, Steady Green means 'Cleared to land'. On the ground, it means 'Cleared for takeoff'.

questions.question: Unless otherwise authorized, what is the maximum indicated airspeed underneath the shelf of Class B airspace?
questions.explanation: FAR 91.117(c) states: No person may operate an aircraft in the airspace underlying a Class B airspace area designated for an airport or in a VFR corridor designated through such a Class B airspace area, at an indicated airspeed of more than 200 knots.

questions.question: What is the transponder requirement for flying over Class C airspace?
options: Mode C transponder is required above the ceiling and lateral boundaries of Class C up to 10,000 feet MSL
No transponder is required above Class C
Mode C is only required within the Class C itself
ADS-B Out is required, but not a transponder
questions.explanation: Unless otherwise authorized, a Mode C transponder is required in and above all Class C airspace up to 10,000 feet MSL. (See FAR 91.215(b)(4))

questions.question: Regarding oxygen requirements (91.211), at what altitude must the required minimum flight crew use supplemental oxygen for the entire duration of the flight?
questions.explanation: Above 14,000 feet MSL (cabin pressure altitude), the required minimum flight crew is required to use supplemental oxygen for the entire flight time at those altitudes. (12,500-14,000 is only after 30 mins).

questions.question: If an instrument currency (6 approaches, holding, intercepting/tracking) expires, how long is the 'grace period' during which a pilot can regain currency with a safety pilot before an IPC is required?
questions.explanation: After the initial 6 months of currency passes, you have a second 6-month period (grace period) to regain currency with a safety pilot/instructor. After that total 12 months (6+6), an Instrument Proficiency Check (IPC) is required.

questions.question: In the METAR code 'R35L/2400V4000FT', what does the 'V' indicate?
questions.explanation: The 'V' indicates 'Variable'. The runway visual range for Runway 35 Left is variable between 2,400 feet and 4,000 feet.

questions.question: If you experience two-way radio communications failure while on an IFR flight plan in VFR conditions, what action should you take?
options: Continue the flight under VFR and land as soon as practicable
Continue the flight according to the filed flight plan
Maintain the highest of the assigned, minimum, or expected altitude
Squawk 7600 and proceed to the alternate airport
questions.explanation: If the failure occurs in VFR conditions, or if VFR conditions are encountered after the failure, each pilot shall continue the flight under VFR and land as soon as practicable.

questions.question: Which transponder code indicates a lost communications situation?
questions.explanation: Code 7600 is used to indicate a lost communications failure. 7500 is for hijacking, and 7700 is for general emergency.

questions.question: When operating VFR in level cruising flight at more than 3,000 feet AGL, on a magnetic course of 175 degrees, what is the appropriate altitude?
options: Any altitude as long as VFR weather minimums are maintained
questions.explanation: On a magnetic course of 0 degrees through 179 degrees (Easterly), fly at an odd thousand foot MSL altitude plus 500 feet.

questions.question: No person may act as a crewmember of a civil aircraft within how many hours after the consumption of any alcoholic beverage?
questions.explanation: FAR 91.17(a) prohibits acting as a crewmember within 8 hours after the consumption of any alcoholic beverage.

questions.question: When two aircraft of different categories are converging at approximately the same altitude (except head-on), which aircraft has the right-of-way?
options: The aircraft to the other's right
The aircraft on a flight plan
questions.explanation: If the aircraft are of different categories, the following applies: Balloon > Glider > Airship > Airplane/Rotorcraft. Generally, the less maneuverable aircraft has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When must aircraft position lights be turned on?
options: From 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise
From end of evening civil twilight to beginning of morning civil twilight
Only when visibility is less than 3 miles
questions.explanation: Position lights are required from sunset to sunrise. This differs from the logging of night flight time (end of civil twilight) or night passenger currency (1 hour after sunset).

questions.question: What is the minimum visibility requirement for VFR flight in Class E airspace at or above 10,000 feet MSL?
questions.explanation: In Class E airspace at or above 10,000 feet MSL, the visibility requirement increases to 5 statute miles.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered 'preventive maintenance' that may be performed by a private pilot?
questions.explanation: Replacing a tire is listed in Part 43 Appendix A(c) as preventive maintenance. Replacing a fuel pump or repairing a prop are generally not.

questions.question: How long is a standard Aircraft Registration Certificate generally valid for?
questions.explanation: Aircraft registration expires three years after the last day of the month in which it was issued.

questions.question: Which of the following incidents requires IMMEDIATE notification to the NTSB?
options: Flight control system malfunction or failure
questions.explanation: NTSB 830.5 requires immediate notification for specific incidents, including flight control system malfunction or failure.
